previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 54-year-old woman with a complex medical history including Crohn’s disease, multiple prior abdominal surgeries, and a history of paralytic ileus presented with abdominal distention, vomiting, and right flank pain. Imaging revealed colonic ileus without obstruction, likely exacerbated by recent opioid use for presumed nephrolithiasis. She was managed conservatively with NG tube decompression, NPO status, IV fluids, and pain control. A urinary tract infection caused by ciprofloxacin-resistant E. coli was identified, and antibiotics were adjusted to nitrofurantoin. Her bowel function gradually improved, allowing NG tube removal and advancement to a regular diet. She remained stable, with resolution of tachycardia and no signs of systemic infection. Blood cultures remained negative. She was discharged home with a plan to complete antibiotics, manage pain and nausea as needed, and follow up with her primary and gastroenterology providers.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ female with Crohn's disease and history of multiple
prior abdominal surgeries complicated by bowel obstruction, now with severe
right-sided abdominal pain, here to evaluate for evidence of bowel
obstruction.

COMPARISON:  Abdominal radiographs, last performed on ___ and CT of the
abdomen and pelvis performed on ___.

FINDINGS:  A single upright and two supine frontal views of the abdomen
demonstrate a nasogastric tube with the tip terminating in the proximal
stomach but the side port located above the diaphragm, likely within the
distal esophagus.  The nasogastric tube should be advanced at least 4 cm for
appropriate positioning.  The patient is status post median sternotomy with
wires appearing intact.  The visualized lung bases are clear.  The bowel gas
pattern is nonspecific with multiple borderline dilated loops of what is
likely large bowel.  Retained oral contrast is present in the distal colon. 
Bowel gas is also present within the stomach.  There is no evidence of free
air beneath the right hemidiaphragm on the upright film.  Suture chain
material is noted in the right lower abdomen consistent with prior bowel
surgery.

IMPRESSION:
1.  NG tube with side port in the distal esophagus needs to be advanced at
least 4 cm to position the side port within the proximal stomach.
2.  Nonspecific gas-filled loops of large bowel with evidence of oral contrast
transit into the rectum from ___.  No evidence of ileus or obstruction at
this time.
